cards.text: Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles in Babylon, is seeing a vision of a new temple (Ezek 1:1-3; 40:2). A man who looks like bronze has been walking him through it, gate by gate (Ezek 40:3). Now the Lord GOD speaks, starting with the gate of the inner court that faces east.

cards.question: The Lord GOD says the inner court's east gate stays shut during the six days of work. So when does it open?

answers.text: On the Sabbath and the New Moon
On Passover and the Day of Atonement
At the start of every harvest

cards.text: Six days shut, then it swings open. Baker, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer waiting for the day it would open, so I am FULLY on this gate's side.
In comes the prince, the leader this vision keeps mentioning (Ezek 44:3). He enters from outside through the gateway's portico and stands by the gatepost.

cards.question: The prince stands by the gatepost while the ___ sacrifice his burnt offerings and peace offerings.
Before the prince departs, what does he do at the threshold of the gate?
On the Sabbath, once the prince departs, the east gate gets shut right away.
That gate stays open until evening. On Sabbaths and New Moons, the ___ of the land also bow in worship before the LORD at the entrance to that gateway.

cards.text: Next comes the offering list: six lambs and a ram on the Sabbath, and on the New Moon a young bull too, all without blemish. Grain and oil go with them, and with the lambs the prince gives as much as he is able, which is EXACTLY how I measure chocolate chips.
When the prince goes in through the gateway's portico, he goes out the same way. But the people at the appointed feasts get a different rule.

cards.question: At the appointed feasts, a worshiper comes in by the north gate. Which gate does he leave by?

cards.text: Nobody goes back out the gate he came in by: in north, out south, in south, out north. It's a one-way hallway, and baker, I have BEEN the guy walking against the whole crowd, mustache first, apologizing to everybody.

cards.question: At the appointed feasts, the prince goes in with the people and leaves when they leave.

cards.text: So the prince is right there in the crowd, in with them and out with them. At the festivals and appointed feasts, the grain offering is an ephah with a bull, an ephah with a ram, and as much as one is able with the lambs.
Now say the prince brings a freewill offering to the LORD, a burnt offering or a peace offering. He's to offer it just as he does on the Sabbath.

cards.question: For the prince's freewill offering, which gate gets opened for him?
After the prince's freewill offering, the gate stays open until evening, just like on the Sabbath.

cards.text: Then comes a rule for every single day: an unblemished year-old lamb as a burnt offering to the LORD every morning. With it goes a grain offering of fine flour moistened with oil.

cards.question: The lamb and the grain offering go up every morning. The Lord GOD calls this a ___ statute.

cards.text: Every morning, the lamb, the grain offering and the oil, a regular burnt offering. Regular as an alarm clock, friend, and unlike me and MY alarm clock, nobody hits snooze on this one.
Now the Lord GOD talks about the prince's land. If the prince gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his sons, it belongs to his descendants as their inheritance.

cards.question: But say the prince gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants instead. What happens to it in the year of freedom?

answers.text: It goes back to the prince
It passes to the servant's sons

cards.text: Back to the prince it goes. His inheritance belongs only to his sons.

cards.question: The prince may take the people's land by evicting them, so he can give it to his sons.
The prince has to give his sons an inheritance from his own property. What does the Lord GOD say this rule is for?

answers.text: So none of His people are displaced from their property
So the prince's sons never argue over who gets the land
So the land around the temple can keep growing larger

cards.text: Then the man guiding Ezekiel brings him through a side entrance into the holy chambers facing north, the ones that belonged to the priests. There, at the far western end, he shows him a place.

cards.question: The man shows Ezekiel a place at the far western end of the priests' holy chambers. What is that place for?

cards.text: The priests boil the guilt offering and the sin offering here, and they BAKE the grain offering. An oven in the temple vision, baker? Give me a second, I'm getting emotional.

cards.question: The priests cook these offerings back in this place so they don't bring them into the outer court and transmit holiness to the people.

cards.text: Then the man brings Ezekiel into the outer court and leads him around to its four corners. In every corner, Ezekiel sees a separate court.

cards.question: The enclosed courts in the four corners of the outer court are each a different size.

cards.text: All four match: forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. Somebody in this vision measures like a baker who LOVES a matching batch.

cards.question: Around the inside of each corner court runs a row of masonry, with ___ built at the base of the walls on all sides.

cards.text: OVENS. On ALL sides. Baker, I just got goosebumps, and I'm a cookie stamper, I don't even HAVE skin.

cards.question: The man tells Ezekiel these are kitchens where those who minister at the temple will cook the sacrifices offered by the ___.

cards.text: Kitchens for the people's sacrifices, cooked by those who minister at the temple. And that's where I'll set the timer for now, friend, because this vision is NOT finished yet.

findings.problem: This story card only restates Ezekiel 46:1, which card 1 told and card 2 just asked (six days shut, then open), and adds a joke. It doesn't move the baker forward. The joke could ride on the next card that tells new verses instead.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The setup says the prince goes out the same way he came in, then says 'the people at the appointed feasts get a different rule.' That tells the baker a worshiper does not leave by the gate he entered, which rules out 'The north gate' on card 11 before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 15 sets up the freewill offering by saying he offers it 'just as he does on the Sabbath,' and the Sabbath gate stays open until evening (card 8). That context points the baker toward True, but the answer is False (Ezekiel 46:12, 'the gate must be closed after he goes out'). A thoughtful baker who reasons from the earlier cards lands on the missed answer.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Ezekiel 46:13-15 is a stretch of offering rules (the daily lamb, a sixth of an ephah, a third of a hin of oil, repeated in v15). It gets three cards (18, 19, 20) and a choice card on its wording ('permanent statute'), when it should be summed up in one story card with no choice card. On card 19, the setup 'every single day' and 'go up every morning' also rules out the wrong answer 'seasonal.'

rule.text: Papa Dorin sums up the stretch in one story card.

findings.problem: Ezekiel 46:16 says the prince gives 'a gift to any of his sons as an inheritance.' The card changes this to a gift 'from his inheritance' to one of his sons. That wording belongs to the servant case in 46:17, and it changes what the text calls the gift.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'An oven in the temple vision, baker?' names ovens before card 13 asks the baker to fill in 'ovens' for the corner courts. Ezekiel 46:20 itself mentions baking but never says 'oven,' so the card also points out a detail the text doesn't state.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'Somebody in this vision measures like a baker who LOVES a matching batch' is mild and pleasant. It isn't a real laugh.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats the answer to card 13 ('OVENS. On ALL sides.') plus a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage. It also repeats the 'I'm getting emotional about ovens' beat from card 8.

The wrong answer 'priests' is arguable. In this same passage the priests sacrifice the prince's offerings (Ezekiel 46:2) and cook offerings (46:20), so a baker could argue the kitchens cook sacrifices offered by the priests.

rule.text: If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
